thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: elevated runtime OOMs on gpu-prod-5..gpu-prod-7 starting 2356004400. Alert rule: runtime.oom_rate > 5/min.

sara: I'm on it — seeing a spike in 5xxs for text-gen endpoints, mostly p95 latency and OOM stack traces in runtime logs. Customers hitting hosted-api in us-west1.

nisha: Logs show repeated failures during attention paging:
```
2026-03-15T02:07:12Z runtime ERROR attention_paged.cpp:431 CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: out of memory
2026-03-15T02:07:12Z runtime WARN kv_cache.cpp:212 free_pages=1200 total_pages=32768 contiguous_free_span=0
2026-03-15T02:07:12Z runtime INFO allocator: attempted_compaction=false last_compact=197h
```
free_pages keeps drifting down, contiguous spans zeroing out — looks like fragmentation not total memory exhaustion.

liam: Customer impact: ~420 requests/min across the cluster; 7% error rate for generation requests, top affected tenant ids: t-143, t-997. p95 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.9s.

maya: Repro on a dev node: small long-running chats with many long contexts increase kv allocations and we see slow page churn. Paging pressure correlates with models that use paged-attention + large KV (>=32k tokens).

liam: Immediate mitigations proposed — pick 2 to run ASAP:
- reduce max_input_tokens for affected routes to 8k (temporary)
- enable aggressive KV eviction (evict watermark -> 0.55)
- fallback routing to smaller attention variant (paged->non-paged where available)
- drain affected nodes and restart runtime containers

sara: Agree. I'll push routing fallback for the PLG tier and reduce max input for non-enterprise tenants now. @ops-doug can you cordon and restart the two flapping nodes (gpu-prod-6, gpu-prod-7)?

ops-doug: On it. Running: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-6
kubectl drain gpu-prod-6 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime -n redwood --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-prod-6
```
Output: node cordoned, pods evicted, runtime pod restarted (pod/runtime-5cd4 restarted).

ops-doug: gpu-prod-7 cordoned and restart queued. Restart logs show `container exited with code 137` for runtime -> likely OOM kill on that pod. Restart succeeded.

nisha: While nodes are being rotated, we should attempt a live compaction sweep on remaining nodes to reclaim fragmented pages. There's a safe runtime flag we can toggle: `KV_COMPACT_ON_ALLOC=1` and run a one-off compaction pass.

kevin: I can roll that via runtime-config API to a small subset of nodes (canary). Command:
```
# enable compact-on-alloc on canary pool
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/runtime/config" -d '{"KV_COMPACT_ON_ALLOC":"1","KV_EVICT_WATERMARK":"0.55"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN"
# trigger compaction
kubectl exec -n redwood runtime-pod-canary -- /usr/local/bin/kv-compact --force --log-level=info
```
Compaction run reclaimed ~1.2GB on the canary node and contiguous spans increased. Recommend rolling config to all non-enterprise pools if canary stable.

liam: Nice — if compaction holds on canary, roll to remaining nodes. Also reduce default batch size on hosted-api to avoid sudden large allocations: set batch_tokens_max=2048 for 15min window.

sara: Rolled routing fallback and reduced max_input_tokens for non-ent. Changes propagated at 2356004505. Error rate dropped from 7% -> 3% within ~3m.

incident-bot: Metric update: runtime.oom_rate down 60% in canary pool. p95 latency improved from 1.9s -> 620ms in canary.

maya: Observed that the allocator's compaction hasn't run for ~197h — we need better guardrails: schedule periodic compaction with threshold (free_pages_ratio < 0.08 triggers async compaction) and a background defrag task. File a follow-up: infra/allocator -> design.

kevin: Logged an ops ticket (#OPS-3492) and a runtime Jira (RUNTIME-1287) for:
- implement auto-compaction on fragmentation threshold
- expose allocator metrics: contiguous_free_spans, compaction_runs, last_compact_ts
- add safety guard to avoid compaction contention with high-traffic windows.

sara: Customer comms — product tried to notify top impacted tenants, engineering to keep status updates. We have one active enterprise outage (t-997) with degraded throughput; CS already escalated.

ops-doug: Post-restart check: running `nvidia-smi` on restarted nodes shows stable GPU mem and lower page-faults. Example:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-80GB         On     | 0000:81:00.0     Off |                  0   |
| 0   8192MiB / 81920MiB |                                    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

nisha: Note: the underlying problem appears to be allocation pattern fragmentation rather than total memory. Long-lived KV segments + many small evictions leave the allocator with many scattered free pages — contiguous allocation for big attention buffers fails -> triggers OOM path.

liam: For immediate policy: default to compact-on-alloc for 2 hours across production pools, then revert and evaluate. Also temporarily block long-context routes > 32k for non-enterprise customers.

sara: I'm handing this to night oncall. @nisha you own the postmortem for allocator fragment root cause, @kevin you own the runtime ticket and canary->prod rollout plan, @ops-doug follow up on node health checks and pod restart automation. I'll update the incident channel with timeline and customer impacts.

incident-bot: Handoff: incident assigned to oncall-night (sara -> liam) at 2356004680. Severity remains Sev2.

liam: Acknowledged. I'll pick up at 2356004700, confirm compaction roll and keep customer-impact dashboard updated.

sara: Thanks everyone. Action items summarized:
- (nisha) produce allocator postmortem + reproducer by EOD
- (kevin) runtime config guard & rollout playbook (OPS-3492)
- (ops-doug) add automated cordon+restart runbook and health-check alert tuning
- (product/CS) targeted customer comms for t-997 and t-143

maya: Logged follow-ups to infra backlog: add compaction metric, auto-trigger policy, and eviction tuning UI in Console.

kevin: I'll keep the `KV_COMPACT_ON_ALLOC` feature toggled for another 90m then start controlled revert if metrics stable.

liam: Monitoring: will watch contiguous_free_spans and p95 for next 2 hours and escalate if error rate increases >1%.

sara: Closing immediate mitigation thread. Will reopen if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
